newsitem.title: CHINA: China's spokesman at Xinhua ends post in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China's spokesman at Xinhua ends post in Hong Kong.

text.p: China's de facto spokesman in Hong Kong said on Thursday his task had been completed once the territory came under Chinese rule earlier this week.

The Beijing-backed China News Service quoted Zhang Junsheng, deputy director of Xinhua News Agency, as saying he ceased to be China's spokesman when Britain withdrew at midnight on Monday, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
Zhang also said Xinhua, or New China News Agency, would not designate a spokesman on Hong Kong affairs.

China opened a Foreign Ministry office in Hong Kong to handle the territory's external affairs and serve as a channel to the central government in Beijing on Tuesday, the first day Hong Kong came under Chinese rule.
